messages:
andrew: Ran an nsys capture on the TRT+vLLM stack during a synthetic workload. Uploading trace: <https://ci.redwood/trace/1749456000>
andrew: TL;DR: engine kernels only ~40% of GPU time. wrapper/device-host copies + scheduler spin/overhead are ~35%. apparent KV cache handoff copies each token.

tasha: can you paste the nsys command you used and which streams were active? curious about capture_range and cuda streams

andrew: used this: ```nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=trt_vllm_run --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --duration=60 python perf_runner.py --seqs 16,64,256``` saw heavy activity on stream 0 and stream 3

kevin: that pattern smells like repeated host->device memcpy for KV cache. Are we serializing KV to host between scheduler and engine? vLLM has a device-side cache option but we might be dropping to host path on wrapper boundaries.

layla: perf-bot flagged a regression earlier today: p95 up ~12% after the recent scheduler change :rotating_light:

perf-bot: Regression alert: job redwood/serving/e2e at 1749130000 — p95 +12% vs baseline. Trace attached: <https://ci.redwood/trace/1749130000>

tasha: two quick checks: 1) are we using pinned host memory for async copies? 2) are we launching kernel with the same stream used for the memcpy? both affect overlap

andrew: enabled pinned host buffers in the wrapper and re-ran; memcpy stall dropped ~60% in the trace but overall p95 still elevated on cold-starts. kernel warmup + engine selection seems to add overhead on first few tokens.

kevin: in the kernels list I see repeated fallbacks: some batches hit `cublasGemmEx` instead of the optimized TRT kernel `trt_engine_invoke`. That suggests TRT engine was created with shape/path that doesn't match dynamic shapes and falls back.

andrew: exactly — suspect kernel selection issues when sequence length varies. TRT builder might be creating multiple engines or doing runtime shape specialization. I saw spikes at engine deserialize/build times in the trace.

layla: can you capture TRT logs? set `TRT_LOGGER=info` and record engine build/deserialization timestamps. also capture `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` for a different view

andrew: plan: run controlled matrix of (seq_len=16/64/256) x (batch=1/4/8) with pinned mem + device-side KV cache enabled, capture nsys and perfetto. also enable `--trt-cache-dir` to reuse engines.

tasha: also instrument scheduler: current loop uses busy-wait for readiness. I saw ~30% CPU time in `vllm::scheduler::poll_loop` in perf output. Replace with condition_variable or at least add `std::this_thread::yield()` so CPU can schedule async memcpy callbacks.

kevin: good point. the wrapper callback currently copies KV to host and then enqueues a host-side task which the scheduler picks up. That handoff is the hotspot.

andrew: reproduced locally, added a patch to avoid host copy for incremental KV (keeping device pointer across calls). branch: `perf/trt-device-kv` — initial run shows tokens/sec +9% and p95 -8% in short runs.

layla: nice. please post the nsys urls and a short before/after table in CI so QA can sanity check outputs. also run evals to ensure output bitwise equivalence isn't assumed if we changed memory layout.

perf-bot: Experiment results: branch perf/trt-device-kv — tokens/sec +9%, p95 -8% on microbench harness. Regression checks passed for top-10 prompts.

tasha: next steps: 1) land pinned mem + device KV changes behind feature flags; 2) add telemetry to count host copies per request; 3) schedule a perf walkthrough next Tue with trace slices.

andrew: opened PR with benchmarks and nsys links: <https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/4321>. uploading perfetto capture for scheduler view: <https://perfetto.redwood/trace/1749456000_sched>

kevin: small follow-up: consider using CUDA graphs for steady-state batches — will eliminate launch overhead for engine invokes once shapes are stable.

andrew: noted. thanks everyone — will follow up with CI-run artifacts and a short playbook for reproducing the regression. :thumbsup:
